messages:
Anya: quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick an admission model for the 'Abuse Shield' integration with quota gateway. TL;DR: tokens (cheap, stateless) vs leases (stateful, fairer). Thoughts?

Mike: I lean leases for fairness — allows eviction, prioritization, and accounting. Tokens amplify noisy bursts.

Lee: Leases add a lot of moving parts at the edge though. Proxy cache, lease renewal, reconcilers. What's the failure-mode plan?

Jordan: Suggestion: hybrid router. Fastpath uses tokens for low-latency/light workloads; heavy tenants cross a threshold and are routed to lease admission. Router decision based on token-burn rate + observed qps.

Anya: that matches my thinking. Also cross-region consistency is the big pain: leases imply some shared state. We could do best-effort local leases + eventual central reconciliation to avoid sync latency.

Mike: local leases + epoch numbers + last-updated tombstones should work. Important: add a "grace drain" window so we don't evict active sessions during rollout/canary.

Lee: Can we keep API surface minimal? Proposal: /admit?mode=token|lease and return {admit:ok, id:<opaque>} . Router maps policy to mode. No schema churn.

Jordan: Ops telemetry needs to be explicit: admitted_by, admit_mode, lease_ttl_ms, denied_reason, fallback_used. Also add a gauge for central-lease-availability. If central down, we MUST fall back to tokens (with a strong penalty).

Anya: perf targets: p50 +1ms for lease path, p99 +5ms. If we can't meet that, revert to tokens for latency-SLO tenants. Migration plan: feature-flagged lease rollout, canary 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100%. Kill switch in console.

Mike: Edge changes to note: persist lease cache (small LRU), renew loop, backpressure when central unavailable. Fallback metric name: admission.fallback_to_token. Critical for postmortem.

Lee: rough policy example (json):
{"threshold_qps": 120, "mode": "lease", "priority": "tierA", "grace_window_ms": 15000}
Router interprets rule order and attaches admit-mode hint to request.

Jordan: owners & timeline: spike (2w) -> prototype (3w) -> canary (2w) -> full rollout. Docs + runbook before canary. Eng-platform: Mike + Lee. Eng-sre: Jordan.

Anya: SGTM. I'll open a focused RFC follow-up doc with checklist (integration tests, chaos tests, telemetry dashboards, runbooks). @ops-bot can you schedule a 30m sync Thu?

ops-bot: ops-bot: Meeting scheduled: Thu 11:00am PT — "Admit-paths scrub". Reminder 24h before.

Mike: :thumbsup: we'll start the spike notes in the shared doc and add perf harness ideas.

Lee: I'll draft the proxy change list and fallback behaviour doc.

Jordan: I'll sketch the dashboards + alert thresholds (fallback rate > 1% triggers pager).

Anya: thanks all — follow-up RFC link incoming when I have it.
